claims.text_en: The unit is a three-way rail knot with a name paradox: BTS Phaya Thai (N2, opened 5 December 1999 with the Sukhumvit Line), ARL Phaya Thai (terminus of the City Line, opened 23 August 2010 'along with a skywalk connecting it to the BTS station'), and an SRT Eastern Line halt dating to 24 January 1907 - all located in Ratchathewi District, not Phaya Thai district. OSM puts the BTS node at 13.75696, 100.53382 and the ARL node at 13.75671, 100.53491 - ~121 m apart.

geography.notes: Wikipedia lead names Ratchathewi District explicitly

evidence.locator: Lead + History (SRT / BTS / Airport Rail Link)
evidence.paraphrase: ARL+BTS+Eastern Line halt in Ratchathewi District; halt 24 Jan 1907; BTS 5 Dec 1999; ARL 23 Aug 2010 with skywalk
~121 m between BTS and ARL nodes

claims.text_en: Anchor offset: the app's '@13.7600-ish' latitude sits ~340 m north of the OSM BTS node (13.75696). The interchange itself is unaffected, but catchment-edge claims toward Victory Monument (which is ~1.4 km from the BTS node in any case) or northward should be checked against the app polygon.

evidence.paraphrase: Latitude difference ~0.0030 deg ~ 340 m

claims.text_en: Transport 10's mechanism: this is the only BTS-ARL meeting point - the ARL City Line's northern terminus feeding the Sukhumvit Line one stop from Siam. City Line fares are 15-45 THB, the airport express has been suspended since September 2014 (all trains stop at all eight stations), and the line is slated to extend from Phaya Thai toward Krung Thep Aphiwat and Don Mueang while also carrying the future Don Mueang-Suvarnabhumi-U-Tapao high-speed rail. Current headways of roughly 10 minutes peak (12-15 off-peak) are snippet-level only.

evidence.paraphrase: Terminus of the ARL City Line; meets Sukhumvit Line
15-45 THB; express suspended since Sep 2014; future extension Phaya Thai to Don Mueang; HSR corridor

claims.text_en: Suan Pakkad Palace Museum is inside the unit: Wikipedia says it is 'located nearby to the east of the station', and OSM places the museum (way 1410385850, open 09:00-16:00) ~364 m east of the BTS node (~307 m by its node). The 1952-opened museum of five traditional Thai houses holds 4,000-year-old Ban Chiang pottery and the 450-year-old Lacquer Pavilion - so the batch-2 '811 m from st.ratchathewi' figure belongs to the district unit, not this station unit.

claims.text_en: 2024-2026 changes around the unit are rail-driven: the SRT halt's tracks are being handed to the Don Mueang-Suvarnabhumi-U-Tapao high-speed project (with the ARL extension Phaya Thai to Don Mueang part of the same programme), and the associated land clearance has been displacing railway-corridor communities along the Rama VI to Phaya Thai stretch - five communities totalling 644 households, with a first-phase 169-household relocation housing project opening its sign at Bueng Makkasan beside Santiphap Park on 29 September 2024. Newer condo stock near the station includes The Extro Phayathai-Rangnam (completed 2025, per listings portal).

question_answers.notes: BTS (1999) + ARL terminus (2010) + SRT Eastern Line halt (1907), ~121 m apart, in Ratchathewi district despite the Phaya Thai name; anchor ~340 m north of the station.
Commuter-junction practicality: interchange flows, hospital and office traffic, street food, quiet evenings.
Transport 10 = unique BTS-ARL interchange + airport line; DE 9 = dense everyday services; rent 5 = mid-band medians matching the app figures.
The safety-5 'test' found no evidence either way; the only documented criticism is of the SRT halt's physical condition.
Peak-hour commuter waves; calmer weekends; low-key evenings.
Skywalk-linked interchange ~121 m platform-to-platform; bus hub one stop north; no sidewalk data found.
Daily-life anchors: street food, Victory Monument institutions one stop north, hospitals and offices along the corridor; Suan Pakkad museum ~364 m east.
App figures (25,000/43,500) match the 800 m 1-BR/2-BR medians (23,450/41,500) closely - one of the best-verified rent sets in this batch, though via flagged portal sources.
1.1 ha park unidentified in OSM; Suan Pakkad's gardens are museum grounds; nearest public park ~1.45 km.
Strong fit: frequent flyers, BTS commuters, value-seekers; poor fit: those wanting leafy quiet or destination nightlife.
Rail-land clearance and the 2024 Bueng Makkasan relocation phase reshape the railway corridor; The Extro Phayathai-Rangnam (2025) adds stock.
Outside the score: no safety data, unidentified park polygon, anchor offset; the name paradox itself (Ratchathewi district) is worth stating on the card.

preview.text_en: Bangkok's BTS-ARL hinge: the Sukhumvit Line meets the airport rail ~120 m platform-to-platform in Ratchathewi district (yes, Phaya Thai station is not in Phaya Thai district), with Suan Pakkad Palace 350 m east and a 1907 SRT halt being rebuilt around a high-speed future.

guide_lead.text_en: Phaya Thai is the city's airport hinge: the ARL City Line terminates here against the BTS Sukhumvit Line (platforms ~121 m apart, skywalk since 2010), one stop from Siam and ~half an hour from Suvarnabhumi. The unit's identity is transport first - the station paradoxically sits in Ratchathewi district - with a practical street life of hospital and office traffic, plentiful food, Suan Pakkad Palace Museum ~350-400 m east inside the unit, and the 1909 Phaya Thai Palace ~1.3 km north, outside the catchment. Rents (25,000/43,500) match the catchment's 1-BR/2-BR medians well. What the score cannot show: no verifiable safety data behind the 5, an unidentified 1.1 ha park polygon, and a railway corridor being progressively cleared for the three-airport high-speed line.

strengths.text_en: The only BTS-ARL interchange in the city core: one-stop Siam access plus a direct airport line, with 800 m catchment rents matching the app's stated figures.
A real heritage-green anchor inside the unit: Suan Pakkad Palace Museum (~350-400 m) with its five traditional houses and 450-year-old Lacquer Pavilion.

tradeoffs.text_en: Safety 5 has no evidence base either way in this pass - it stays an unanchored dataset value rather than a documented condition.
The green story is thinner than the 8 suggests: no named public park inside the catchment was found, and the 1.1 ha polygon is unmatched (Suan Pakkad's grounds are a ticketed museum).

day_night.text_en: The interchange dominates mornings and evenings with commuter and airport flows; midday belongs to hospital/office errands and food stalls; evenings and weekends are low-key.

within_area_variation.text_en: The station-and-skywalk block is the loudest node; the Si Ayutthaya/Suan Pakkad side east is calmer, and the SRT/rail-corridor edge west carries the clearance works.

conditional_fit.text_en: Strong fit: frequent flyers and BTS commuters priced out of Siam/Ratchathewi proper - the rent medians here are the interchange's own.
Poor fit: households wanting leafy park-side living or destination nightlife; neither exists in this catchment.

uncertainties: rating safety (5): no unit-level statistics found; unanchored in this pass (phaya-thai-st-c07).
Park identity: the app's 1.1 ha polygon did not match any named OSM park within 900 m of the stations (phaya-thai-st-c09).
Anchor sits ~340 m north of the BTS node; edge memberships toward Victory Monument need polygon re-check (phaya-thai-st-c02).
ARL headway (~10 min peak) is snippet-level only; the Wikipedia body documents fares and the 2014 express suspension but not current headways (phaya-thai-st-c03).
Railway-corridor displacement affects the corridor generally; overlap with this specific Voronoi cell is undetermined (phaya-thai-st-c11).
